land.text: Volhynia, held by Roman from 1197 (Roman page: 'Volhynia (1170-1189; 1189-1205)')

predecessors.note: Kingdom page infobox: 'Preceded by' the Principality of Galicia and the Principality of Volhynia. Cliopatria's Volhynia row runs to 1201, two years past the union.

land.text: Galicia, taken by Roman in 1199 after the death of Prince Vladimir II Yaroslavich

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Halych row runs to 1201, two years past the union (double-drawn 1199-1201 unless the Halych dossier ends at 1199).

land.text: Galicia, 'captured and annexed' by Casimir III in 1349 and 'transferred to the Polish Crown'

successors.note: Przemysl had gone to Poland already in the 1344 treaty.

land.text: Volhynia 'went to Lithuania' (Liubartas) in 1349 on the Kingdom page; the Wars page has Liubartas holding Volhynia from 1344 and Casimir and Louis taking its west in 1348

successors.note: Eastern Volhynia with Lutsk stayed with Liubartas until at least 1366 (Wars page).

capitals.name: Halych
capitals.note: 'Roman captured Kiev [1200] but kept Halych as his capital' (Kingdom page); Daniel and Vasylko moved the capital from Halych to Kholm 'in late 1240 or early 1241' (Daniel page). Volodymyr was the seat in Volhynia (infobox lists Volodymyr and Halych without dates).

capitals.name: Lviv
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Lviv (1272-1301)'; 'Lev I moved the capital from Chelm to Lviv' in 1272.

capitals.name: Volodymyr (Volodymyr-Volynskyi)
capitals.note: Reading: the infobox ends Lviv in 1301; the Yuri I page names Volodymyr as the capital without a date and the Yuri II page says that in 1324 'Yuri granted city rights to Volodymyr, where he established his court'. After Casimir took Lviv in June 1340 (Wars page) no page names a seat.

rulers.name: Roman the Great (Roman Mstyslavych)
rulers.title: Prince of Galicia and Volhynia
rulers.note: Kingdom page infobox: 'Roman the Great, 1199-1205'; killed at the Battle of Zawichost in 1205.

rulers.name: Daniel (Danylo Romanovych)
rulers.title: Prince of Volhynia and Galicia
rulers.note: Daniel page infobox: Prince of Volhynia 1205-1206 and 1215-1238; Prince of Galicia 1205-1206, 1211-1213, 1230-1232, 1233-1234, 1238-1266. Added by the reviewer (eu-16-e) to close the 1205-1238 gap in the strip.

rulers.name: Alexander of Belz
rulers.title: Prince of Volhynia (Volodymyr)
rulers.note: Daniel page infobox: Alexander of Belz succeeds Daniel as Prince of Volhynia in 1206 and precedes him in 1215; 'In 1215, at the insistence of Leszek the White, Alexander of Belz was forced to return Volodymyr to Daniel.' Added by the reviewer (eu-16-e).

rulers.name: Daniel (Danylo Romanovych)
rulers.title: Prince of Volhynia
rulers.note: Daniel page infobox: Prince of Volhynia 1215-1238; Galicia only in 1211-1213 and 1230-1232 (ledger). Added by the reviewer (eu-16-e).

rulers.name: Daniel (Danylo Romanovych)
rulers.title: Prince, from 1253 King of Ruthenia
rulers.note: Page: 'Daniel, 1238-1264 (crowned king 1253-1264)'. The Daniel page dates his death to 1266 and says 1264 rests on an erroneous chronology. 1205-1237 has no single ruler of the whole state: Galicia passed between the Igorevichi, Kormylchych, Hungarian princes, Mstislav and Chernigov's princes while Daniel held Volhynia in part.

rulers.name: Lev I (Leo I)
rulers.note: Kingdom page: 'Lev I, 1264-1301'; the Leo page's infobox gives King of Ruthenia 1269-1301.

rulers.name: Andrew and Lev II (joint rule)
rulers.title: Kings of Galicia-Volhynia
rulers.note: 'Andrew and Lev II jointly ruled and proclaimed themselves kings'; died together in battle against the Mongols in 1323 without heirs, ending the Rurikid line.

rulers.name: Yuri II Boleslav (Boleslaw-Yuri II)
rulers.title: Prince and dominus of Ruthenia
rulers.note: Kingdom page 1323-1340; the Yuri II page gives 1323/1325-1340 and an April 1340 death by poison. A Piast (Masovian) prince who converted to Orthodoxy.

rulers.name: Liubartas (Lubart)
rulers.note: Infobox: 'Liubartas, 1341-1349' as last ruler; Dmytro Dedko was de facto ruler 1323-1349 and accepted Polish overlordship as starost of Galicia in summer 1341.

correction.text: Roman's Galicia and Volhynia after the union of 1199: Cliopatria's 1202 shape carried back three years

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1202 but the page dates the union to 1199 ('Roman held Volhynia from 1197 and Galicia from 1199'). The shape of 1202 is used unchanged. Cliopatria's Halych and Volhynia rows still run to 1201, so 1199-1201 is double-drawn unless their dossiers end in 1199.

188,420 km2 for 1202-1205: Roman's Galicia and Volhynia after the 1199 union. The Kingdom page gives no area, so there is nothing to compare. Kiev (1200-1203, 1204-1205) and Pereyaslavl (1203-1205) were held through subordinates and are carried as vassal events, not in the shape. The Cuman campaigns of 1201-02 and 1203-04 gained no land on the page.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Galicia: after Roman's death in 1205 'the boyars of Galicia forced the four-year-old Daniel into exile' (Daniel page); the three sons of Igor Svyatoslavich controlled Galicia 1206-1212 (Kingdom page). Volhynia stays as drawn

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps Roman's whole realm for 1206-1209 (188,285 km2). The pages put Galicia in other hands: Daniel page 1205 exile, Kingdom page 1206-1212 Igorevichi, Roman page 'the throne went to Vladimir III Igorevich'. Volhynia was also split among Rurikid relatives in these years (Daniel regained Volodymyr only in 1215, Daniel page); that is not modelled and the Volhynia part of the shape stays.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1210 shape without Galicia at 1210; the ledger returns Galicia to Daniel in September 1211 ('this army restored the nine-year-old prince to the throne') and takes it away again in 1213

keyframe_review.note: 188,420 km2 drawn for 1210-1215 against a Galicia that changed hands in 1211 and 1213/14 and was partitioned by Hungary and Poland in 1214 (Kingdom page: 'Hungary and Poland partitioned the Galician lands by compromise'). The correction is the base shape; the ledger carries 1211 and 1213.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Galicia: 'Hungarian occupation under sons of Andrew II. Coloman ruled 1214-1220, and Andrew ruled 1220-1232' (Kingdom page)

keyframe_review.note: The shape keeps Galicia in Daniel's realm while the page has Hungarian princes in Halych (1214-1220 Coloman); Daniel renounced his claim to Galicia in 1219 in favour of Mstislav the Bold (Daniel page). Volodymyr was returned to Daniel in 1215 (Daniel page).

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Galicia: 'Mstislav the Able led an uprising and ruled Galicia from 1221 to 1228' (Kingdom page); Hungarian prince Andrew held it 1220-1232 on the same page

keyframe_review.note: 1220-1226 draws Roman's whole realm; the page has Galicia under Coloman/Andrew of Hungary and then Mstislav the Able (1221-1228), the Daniel page calls him Mstislav the Bold and has Daniel marry his daughter in 1219. The two timelines on the Kingdom page overlap and are not reconciled there.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Galicia at 1227: in 1228 'the boyars expelled Mstislav and transferred Galicia to the king of Hungary' (Kingdom page); Daniel held Halych only in 1230-1232 (Daniel page)

keyframe_review.note: The ledger carries Daniel's brief hold of Galicia in 1230-1232 (Daniel page: invited to Halych in 1230, Hungarian prince Andrew retook it in 1232). The Kingdom page says instead that Daniel failed to retake Galicia in 1230-1232 and 1233-1235 but held Volhynia; the pages disagree and both are in the notes.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without Galicia at 1236: 'children of Michael of Chernigov ruled' Galicia 1235-1238; in 1238 'Daniel conquered Galicia with burgher support, reunited it with Volhynia'

keyframe_review.note: 188,376 km2 drawn for 1236-1240. The 1238 gain (most of Galicia including the capital) and the 1245 gain of the rest are in the ledger; the 1236-1237 years have Galicia under Chernigov's princes. Kiev (1239-1240) was held as a vassal and is not in the shape.

correction.text: Daniel's realm after the Mongol raid of 1240-41: the 1240 shape without the Przemysl land, which Daniel took only after the battle at Yaroslav in August 1245 ('He then took the rest of Galicia')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Galicia-Volhynia shape for 1241-1293 (the Mongol decades). Batu 'ravaged much of Galicia-Volhynia despite Daniel's fierce resistance' but the page does not say the principality was occupied; it kept its princes and paid tribute 'until well into the 14th century'. The shape is Cliopatria's own 1240 shape carried forward (Daniel page: Halych destroyed in April 1241, capital moved to Kholm); the page draws no boundary. Przemysl is my reading of 'the rest of Galicia'.

minus.text: the part of the 1240 shape that lies in Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape of 1260 and is outside the 1294 shape

correction.text: The 1240 shape without the eastern lands that the 1294 shape no longer has and the Mongol Empire shape of 1260 covers (about 211 cells): in 1260 'Boroldai's large army forced Daniel to accept Mongol authority and raze his remaining fortifications' (Kingdom page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence low: no page says which land the Mongols took. Cliopatria's 1294 Galicia-Volhynia shape has 310 cells fewer than its 1240 shape; 211 of them lie in the Mongol/Golden Horde shape and 99 in the Lithuanian shape. The 1260 date is the page's Boroldai sentence (and the Daniel page's 'in 1259, a Mongol force under Burundai and Nogai Khan entered Galicia and Volhynia'). The Lithuanian part is lost in 1276.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1294 shape without the Lublin region (gained 1292) and Transcarpathia (annexed 1280): Galicia, Volhynia and Chelm after the Lithuanian war of 1274-1276

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1274-1276, Leo fought a war against the new Lithuanian ruler, Traidenis, but was defeated'; Lithuania 'took Black Ruthenia and Navahrudak' (no year on the page). The shape is the 1294 shape minus the two later additions.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1294 shape without the Lublin region: with the part of Carpathian Ruthenia including Mukachevo that Leo 'temporarily annexed' in 1280 (the page notes some historians dispute it)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Kingdom page says 'claims that he annexed Transcarpathian areas, including Munkacs, lack firm evidence'; the Leo page says he did, temporarily. Cliopatria's 1294 shape contains Uzhhorod, so the annexation is kept as disputed.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1294 shape carried back two years: Lev 'extended his influence into the Lublin region' in 1292 (Kingdom page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page says 'influence', not annexation; Cliopatria draws Lublin inside the 1294 shape and the Duchy of Sandomierz shape covers the Lublin area to 1304, so the 1294-1301 Lublin part is soft.

132,428 km2 for 1294-1304 (Galicia, Volhynia, Chelm, the Lublin region and Transcarpathia). 'At the time of Leo's death in 1301, the state of Galicia-Volhynia was at the height of its power' (Leo page). The Transcarpathian part is disputed (Kingdom page: no firm evidence; Leo page: annexed temporarily in 1280) and the Lublin part is 'influence' from 1292; both go in 1301/1302. No area on the pages to compare.

112,376 km2: the 1294 shape without Lublin ('1302: Yuri I lost Lublin to the Poles') and Transcarpathia ('probably returned to Hungary after Leo's death', Leo page; a Hungarian castle taken from the last Galician garrison in 1322 on the same page). Cliopatria steps in 1305, three years after the page's 1302.
112,286 km2, 90 km2 less than 1305: no page dates a change in 1314 and none is claimed. Andrew and Lev II rule jointly 1308-1323 as kings 'tributary to the Mongols'.

82,924 km2: the 1314 shape without the northern strip (Brest, Berestia, Drohiczyn), which Cliopatria's Lithuanian shape covers from 1326; no page dates that loss (the Kingdom page lists Berestia as an appanage without a date). The shape keeps Volodymyr and Lutsk, which agrees with the Yuri II page ('ruler over Ruthenia (Galicia and Volynia)', court at Volodymyr from 1324) and disagrees with the Kingdom page's sentence that in 1323 'Volhynia passed to Liubartas (Lithuania)'. The shape is kept and the disagreement noted.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1344 shape without the Principality of Peremyshl, which 'a treaty gave ... to the Crown of Poland' in 1344; the kingdom ends in 1349, so the shape holds for 1344-1349 only

keyframe_review.note: 82,924 km2, identical to 1326, so Cliopatria shows nothing for the 1344 treaty; the Kingdom page gives Peremyshl to Poland and 'the rest' to Liubartas, the Wars page gives Galicia to Casimir and Volhynia to Liubartas. Cliopatria runs the row to 1351, the Kingdom page's infobox ends the kingdom with the transfer of Galicia to Poland in 1349, so 1350-1351 is dropped. Both pages put Galicia under Polish pressure from 1340 (Lviv taken June 1340).

region.text: Galicia and Volhynia under Roman, drawn as Cliopatria's 1202 shape

ledger.note: 1199: Roman unites Galicia and Volhynia. 'Roman held Volhynia from 1197 and Galicia from 1199. Vladimir II Yaroslavich, the last Prince of Galicia, died in 1198 or 1199 without a recognized paternal heir, and Roman united the lands in 1199 at the Galician boyars' invitation.' The Roman page agrees: 'In 1199, after the death of Prince Volodymyr Yaroslavych of Halych, Roman took the Galician throne a second time, creating the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia.'

region.text: the Kiev principality, ruled through subordinates

ledger.note: 1200: Roman takes Kiev. 'Roman captured Kiev but kept Halych as his capital and installed subordinates to rule Kiev.' The Roman page puts the capture within the Cuman campaigns of 1201-1204 and names Rostislav, his brother-in-law, as the prince installed.
1203: Kiev lost. 'While he was away, Rurik II sacked Kiev with Polovtsian (Cuman) and Chernihivian help.'

region.text: 'Roman extended his rule to the Principality of Pereyaslavl'

ledger.note: 1203: Roman extends his rule to the Principality of Pereyaslavl.
1204: Roman retakes Kiev, 'the height of his reign'.
1205: Roman killed at Zawichost; his hold on Kiev ends with him. The page does not say when Kiev was lost; it says only that his death 'started a succession war and about 40 years of chaos'.
1205: Pereyaslavl lapses with Roman's death; the page is silent on when it was lost.

region.text: Galicia (Halych), where the boyars expelled Daniel

ledger.note: 1205: Galicia lost. 'After his death in 1205, the boyars of Galicia forced the four-year-old Daniel into exile.' The Kingdom page has the three sons of Igor Svyatoslavich controlling Galicia 1206-1212; the Roman page says 'the throne went to Vladimir III Igorevich'.

September 1211: Daniel restored in Halych. 'In 1210 a united army composed of Hungarians and Galicians invaded the principality'; in September 1211 it 'restored the nine-year-old prince to the throne'. The Kingdom page has Mstislav the Mute as regent for Daniel in 1211-1212 and the Igorevichi to 1212.

region.text: Galicia, under Kormylchych and then Hungarian princes

ledger.note: 1213: Galicia lost again. A boyar uprising 1212-1214 led by Volodyslav Kormylchych, who 'assumed the Galician throne in 1213 or 1214', the only non-Rurikid to rule a Rus' principality; the Daniel page infobox gives Daniel Galicia 1211-1213. In 1214 Hungary and Poland partitioned the Galician lands, and Hungarian princes held them 1214-1232 (Coloman 1214-1220, Andrew 1220-1232).

1230: Daniel takes Halych a second time. 'In 1230 Daniel was invited to take the throne of Halych for the second time' and he 'defeated Hungarian troops besieging the city'. The Kingdom page says instead that he failed to retake Galicia in 1230-1232 and 1233-1235; the Daniel page infobox gives him Galicia 1230-1232 and 1233-1234.

region.text: Galicia, retaken by Prince Andrew of Hungary

ledger.note: 1232: Halych lost to Hungary. The boyars 'helped Hungarian prince Andrew to recapture the city in 1232'. In 1235-1238 Galicia was ruled by the children of Michael of Chernigov (Kingdom page).

1238: Daniel conquers Galicia and reunites it with Volhynia. 'Daniel conquered Galicia with burgher support, reunited it with Volhynia, and ruled until 1264.' The Daniel page says he 'regained most of Galicia, including the capital'; Przemysl is left for 1245. The children of Michael of Chernigov had ruled it 1235-1238.

region.text: the Kiev principality, held through Voivode Dmytro

ledger.note: 1239: Daniel takes Kiev. 'Daniel captured Kiev and placed Voivode Dmytro in charge.' The Mongol invasion page says he 'took Kiev under his protection' the year before its fall; the Daniel page has Michael of Chernigov flee and Daniel send his voivode to defend the city.
December 1240: Kiev falls to the Mongols. 'The horde stormed Kiev in December 1240' (the Daniel page gives 6 December). The conqueror is the Mongol Empire.

1241: the capital moves from Halych to Kholm. Daniel and Vasylko moved it 'in late 1240 or early 1241'; in April 1241 the Mongols passed through Galicia and Volhynia, destroying Halych, and Daniel fled to Poland.

region.text: the rest of Galicia after Yaroslav (reading: the Przemysl land)

ledger.note: August 1245: Daniel takes the rest of Galicia. 'On 17 August 1245, Daniel defeated a combined force of the prince of Chernigov' at Yaroslav; 'He then took the rest of Galicia.' The Kingdom page adds that Daniel and Vasylko defeated Polish and Hungarian forces there. Przemysl is my reading of 'the rest'.

1253: Daniel crowned King of Ruthenia. 'Papal legate Opizo de Mezzano crowned Daniel the first King of Ruthenia (Rex Russiae) at Dorohochyn (Drohiczyn).' The principality becomes a kingdom; colour and dossier continue. Since winter 1245-1246, when Daniel went to Sarai and 'submitted to Batu Khan as a vassal', the realm paid tribute to the Golden Horde (infobox: vassal 1246-1253; text: 'tributary to the Mongols' to 1349); that vassalage belongs to the Mongol/Golden Horde dossiers.

region.text: eastern lands of the 1240 shape that Cliopatria gives to the Mongol Empire / Golden Horde, outside the 1294 shape (page silent)

ledger.note: 1260: Mongol authority imposed. 'Boroldai's large army forced Daniel to accept Mongol authority and raze his remaining fortifications.' The page names no land; the eastern lands missing from Cliopatria's 1294 shape and covered by the Mongol shape are taken here as the loss (bridging judgment).
1272: Lev I moves the capital from Chelm to Lviv (infobox: Lviv 1272-1301).

region.text: the part of the 1240 shape that Cliopatria's 1294 Lithuanian shape covers (reading of 'Black Ruthenia and Navahrudak')

ledger.note: 1276: Lithuania takes Black Ruthenia. 'In 1274-1276, Leo fought a war against the new Lithuanian ruler, Traidenis, but was defeated'; Lithuania took Black Ruthenia and Navahrudak (the page gives no year or boundary). The lost land is read from Cliopatria: the 99 cells of the 1240 shape that are outside the 1294 shape and inside the Lithuanian shape.

region.text: part of Carpathian Ruthenia including Mukachevo

ledger.note: 1280: Leo annexes part of Carpathian Ruthenia. 'Leo defeated the Kingdom of Hungary and temporarily annexed part of Carpathian Ruthenia, including the town of Mukachevo.' The Leo page notes that some historians dispute it; the Kingdom page says the claim lacks firm evidence. A 1299 document calls him 'Duke of Ruthenians'.

1292: Lev reaches into the Lublin region. 'Lev took advantage of Polish fragmentation and extended his influence into the Lublin region'; the Land of Chelm is later part of the Lublin region (1289-1302). 'Influence' is the page's word.

1301: Transcarpathia back to Hungary. 'Carpathian Ruthenia probably returned to Hungary after Leo's death' in 1301; a Hungarian document of 1307 mentions no Galician princes and 'the last Galician garrison in the region lost its castle to Hungarians in 1322'.
1302: Yuri I loses Lublin. 'Yuri I lost Lublin to the Poles.' Cliopatria's Duchy of Sandomierz shape covers the Lublin area to 1304.

The seat passes from Lviv to Volodymyr after Lev I's death. The Kingdom page infobox ends Lviv in 1301; the Yuri I page names Volodymyr as the capital without a date; Yuri II established his court there in 1324.

1323: the Rurikid line ends. 'Andrew and Lev II died together in battle against the Mongols and left no heirs'; Yuri II Boleslav, a Polish (Masovian) prince and grandson of Yuri I, rules from 1323 (Yuri II page: 1323/1325). The Kingdom page adds that Volhynia 'passed to Liubartas (Lithuania)' and the boyars took control of Galicia; the Yuri II page has him ruling both from Volodymyr, so Volhynia stays in the state here.

region.text: the strip of Berestia (Brest, Drohiczyn) in the 1314 shape and not the 1326 one

ledger.note: 1326: the northern strip goes to Lithuania. No page dates it; Cliopatria's Galicia-Volhynia shape drops Brest, Berestia and Drohiczyn in 1326 and Cliopatria's Lithuanian shape covers 126 of those 128 cells from that year.

June 1340: Casimir III takes Lviv. Yuri II Boleslav was poisoned in April 1340; Casimir 'returned with a larger army, took Lviv, and burned the Lviv High Castle'. In summer 1341 Detko accepted Polish overlordship as starost of Galicia (Kingdom page), and Liubartas claimed the throne.

1344: Peremyshl goes to Poland. 'A treaty gave the Principality of Peremyshl to the Crown of Poland, while the rest went to Liubartas.' The Wars page words the same treaty as 'Volhynia went to Liubartas and Galicia to Casimir'.
1349: Casimir III annexes Galicia. 'Casimir III captured and annexed Galicia, and Galicia was transferred to the Polish Crown.'
1349: Galicia passes to the Polish Crown (infobox: 'Transfer of Galicia to the Polish Crown, 1349'); the vassalage to the Golden Horde ended.

region.text: Volhynia (Volodymyr, Lutsk) and the Land of Chelm: the rest of the 1344 shape once Galicia is taken out

ledger.note: 1349: Volhynia goes to Lithuania. 'Volhynia went to Lithuania.' The Wars page is more tangled: Liubartas lost all but eastern Volhynia with Lutsk to Casimir and Louis I in 1348, and an autumn 1352 truce gave him Volhynia, Podolia, Belz and Chelm.

region.text: the remainder of the kingdom: Galicia and Volhynia

ledger.note: 1349: the Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia ends. Galicia goes to the Polish Crown and Volhynia to Lithuania; the Wars page dates the 'fall of the Kingdom' inside the 1340-1392 wars and the final partition to the Ostrow agreement of 1392 (Poland Galicia, Lithuania Volhynia).

wars.name: Roman's Cuman campaigns
wars.outcome: 'In 1201-1202 and 1203-1204 Roman led two successful campaigns against the Cumans'; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: War of the Galician Succession
wars.outcome: Roman's death in 1205 began the war 'in 1205 and ran to 1245' (Roman page). Galicia passed between boyars, the Igorevichi, Hungarian and Polish princes, Mstislav the Able and Chernigov's princes until Daniel took Halych in 1238 and the rest after the battle at Yaroslav on 17 August 1245.
wars.note: The war's own Wikipedia article would not load (War_of_the_Galician_Succession and War_of_Galician_Succession both url_not_found, as did Battle_of_Yaroslav_(1245)); the dated steps are from the Kingdom and Daniel pages. The ledger holds the transfers of Galicia.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'

zones.text: Kiev, held by Daniel's voivode Dmytro 1239-1240

wars.outcome: Mongol victory; Kiev stormed in December 1240. Galicia-Volhynia was ravaged but not occupied and was forced to accept Mongol supremacy and pay tribute 'until well into the 14th century'.

wars.name: Daniel's wars with Kuremsa and Burundai

zones.text: lands east of the 1294 shape that pass to the Mongol shape (page silent)

wars.outcome: Daniel drove the Mongols out of Volhynia in 1256 and held Lutsk and Volodymyr in 1257, but in 1259-1260 Burundai's and Boroldai's armies made him pull down his fortifications and accept Mongol authority.
wars.note: The Daniel page dates Kuremsa's assaults to 1254 ('the following year') and Burundai's entry to 1259.

wars.name: Lithuanian-Galician war of 1274-1276

zones.text: Black Ruthenia with Navahrudak, read from Cliopatria's Lithuanian shape

wars.outcome: 'Leo fought a war against the new Lithuanian ruler, Traidenis, but was defeated'; Lithuania took Black Ruthenia and Navahrudak.

wars.name: Leo's campaigns against Poland and Hungary

zones.text: part of Carpathian Ruthenia including Mukachevo, temporarily annexed (disputed)

wars.outcome: In 1279 Leo allied with Wenceslaus II of Bohemia and invaded Poland; the attempt on Krakow failed in 1280. In 1280 he defeated Hungary and temporarily annexed part of Carpathian Ruthenia.

wars.name: Galicia-Volhynia Wars

zones.text: Galicia, taken by Casimir in 1340 and annexed in 1349

wars.outcome: Fall of the Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia: Casimir took Lviv in June 1340; a 1344 treaty gave Galicia to Casimir and Volhynia to Liubartas; Poland took Galicia (1349 on the Kingdom page), Hungary held it 1370-1387, and the 1392 Ostrow agreement left Poland Galicia and Lithuania Volhynia.
wars.note: This dossier ends in 1349 on the Kingdom page's infobox; the war runs on to 1392.

certainty.note: No border of the kingdom is given by a survey or a line on any page opened; the Peremyshl cut of 1344 and the 1302 loss of Lublin are named by treaty or event but without boundaries. Frontiers with the steppe, the Pripyat marshes, Lithuania and the Polish duchies are approximate throughout.
